sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces adopted a new concentrated strike tactic, focusing cruise missiles on up to three targets with relatively few drones, which may precede a massive UAV wave on western Ukraine. Continuous Shahed and Geran-5 launches from multiple axes—Chernihiv, Kirovohrad, Donetsk, Mykolaiv, Black Sea—target Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Vinnytsia, and Cherkasy. Ukrainian power infrastructure remains vulnerable, with UAV debris causing outages in Kyiv. The combination of reduced drone numbers and concentrated missiles suggests Russian forces are conserving assets for a larger operational wave.
sections.regional_response: The EU allocated €1.24 billion for drones and missiles and agreed on a 22nd sanctions package targeting over 1,500 defense-sector entities, while von der Leyen condemned attacks on civilian Black Sea vessels. NATO's Military Committee visited Kyiv for the first time in eight years, affirming support and discussing military priorities with Commander Drapaty. On the diplomatic front, Trump stated the war is nearing end and will soon speak with Putin, while Ukraine's Vereshchuk insisted no peace is foreseeable, and Kyiv declared readiness for all truce options.
sections.intelligence_notes: Russian concentration of cruise missiles on limited targets with reduced drone usage signals preparation for a large-scale UAV strike on western Ukraine; continuous reactive Shahed launches from all axes indicate sustained pressure on Ukrainian air defenses. Ukrainian infrastructure faces repeated strikes—Kyiv cardboard plant hit third time, Kremenchuk industrial facility struck, power lines damaged. Economic losses exceed 100 billion hryvnias. The NATO Military Committee visit and EU funding suggest Western military prioritization will continue despite political noise about peace.
